data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N
 
TRADE: 

Japan's tariff negotiator Akazawa is arranging his eighth visit to the US for trade talks as early as this weekend. (Asahi)

The EU is blocking the UK government's attempts to join a pan-European trading bloc to reduce post-Brexit supply chain challenges for goods exporters, according to the FT citing officials. (FT)

MACRO:

US Treasury Secretary Bessent said in a Fox interview he believes the Federal Reserve could lower interest rates by September. (Fox)

Manhattan home sales in the second quarter were stronger than they’ve been in almost two years, boosted by cash buyers undeterred by the economic uncertainty created by Trump’s trade war. (BBG)

Chinese provinces are implementing Beijing’s directive to broaden the use of funds raised through special local bond issuance, extending their application to areas such as the purchase of unsold homes and the repayment of corporate debts. (Shanghai Securities News)

HKMA intervenes as HK dollar hits weak end of range. (RTRS)

European junk bond sales hit record as investors cut US exposure. (FT)

Australian retail sales barely grew for a fourth straight month in May as gains in clothing purchases were offset by a rare drop in food sales, bolstering the case for another cut in rates next week. (RTRS)

Roadblocks by informal miners are disrupting transport of copper from some mines in Peru, including those owned by MMG Ltd. and Hudbay Minerals Inc., according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Trump posted on Truth, "My Representatives had a long and productive meeting with the Israelis today on Gaza. Israel has agreed to the necessary conditions to finalize the 60 Day CEASEFIRE, during which time we will work with all parties to end the War..." (Truth Social)

Some of China’s largest ports have received Iranian crude this year, supporting a multi-billion oil trade and highlighting a significant gap in US efforts to curb funds for Tehran’s military and to uphold existing sanctions. (BBG)

The U.S. has stopped the delivery of air-defense interceptors and other weapons intended for Ukraine and is using them instead to beef up Pentagon stocks, a Trump administration official and two congressional aides said Tuesday. (WSJ)

Israel urged China to use its economic and political sway to rein in Iran’s military and nuclear ambitions. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

U.S. banking giants announced plans on Tuesday to raise their third-quarter dividends after clearing the Federal Reserve's annual health check last week. (RTRS)

JPMorgan Chase, after completing its stress tests, boosted its quarterly dividend and authorized a new $50 billion share repurchase program. (WSJ)

Intel's new chief executive is exploring a big change to its contract manufacturing business to win major customers, according to Reuters sources, in a potentially expensive shift from his predecessor's plans. (RTRS)

Apple appears to have halted development of its foldable iPad. (DigiTimes)

'China Is Quickly Eroding America’s Lead in the Global AI Race' WSJ article notes Chinese AI models are becoming more popular worldwide, testing American superiority. (WSJ)

The FTC has launched an in-depth investigation into SoftBank Group's purchase of semiconductor designer Ampere Computing LLC. (Bloomberg)

Constellation Brands posted lower profit and sales in its most recent quarter, as widespread consumer weakness, including among its core Hispanic demographic, continued to weigh on sales of beer and wine. (WSJ)

Paramount Global said it has agreed in principle to pay $16 million to settle a lawsuit with President Trump over a “60 Minutes” interview with former Vice President Kamala Harris. (WSJ)

Mainland China investors offloaded a combined HK$46.4 billion ($5.9 billion) worth of Tencent, Xiaomi, and Alibaba shares through the trading links with the financial hub in June, according to Bloomberg calculations based on exchange data. They were also net sellers of the three stocks in May. (BBG)

Alibaba is offering 50 billion yuan ($7 billion) of subsidies for food deliveries and online retail to boost its instant commerce business in China as competition heats up. (BBG)

Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. is adding new data centers in Malaysia and the Philippines in pursuit of AI-driven growth. (BBG)

According to DigiTimes Research, Huawei is expected to ship 800,000 AI accelerators this year. (DigiTimes via @Jukanlosreve)

Listings in Hong Kong hit the highest since December 2022 last month, as a rally in the Asian financial hub’s stocks drove a rush for share sales. (BBG)

Deutsche Bank has laid out a steeper than expected capital hit from new rules on how banks calculate risk, as European lenders begin to reveal the impact of Basel IV reforms. (FT)

DATA RECAP (Newsquawk)

Australian Retail Sales MM Final (May) 0.2% vs. Exp. 0.4% (Prev. -0.1%)
Australian Building Approvals (May) 3.2% vs. Exp. 4.8% (Prev. -5.7%, Rev. -4.1%)
South Korean CPI MM (Jun) 0.0% vs. Exp. 0.0% (Prev. -0.1%)
South Korean CPI Growth YY (Jun) 2.2% vs. Exp. 2.1% (Prev. 1.9%)
